title: Why Is SoFi Stock Crashing, and is it a Generational Buying Opportunity?
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: SoFi (SOFI) is down 12% in a month and over 46% in 2026, mainly on higher interest rates. Parkevtate walks through the rate headwinds: the fair value of SoFi's $46.6bn loan book likely falls by billions, and default rates (personal loans 4.57% to 4.77% Mar-Jun, student 0.69% to 0.73%) likely rose again as consumers weaken, oil stays high and white-collar layoffs rise — partly offset by a booming lending business (Q2 lending segment revenue +63% YoY, strong third-party loan sales). At $15 and a forward P/E of 18.5 he updates his fair value to $19 (>24% upside over 12-18 months) and ranks it a buying opportunity — his first tracked SOFI call — while calling it above-average risk. He will cover Netflix earnings live for members on Tue 20 Oct.

calls.base_case: Lending segment booming (Q2 segment revenue +63% YoY) with strong third-party loan demand.
calls.bear_case: Higher rates cut the fair value of its $46.6bn loan book (likely billions), default rates rising (personal loans 4.57%->4.77% Mar-Jun) and likely up again; consumer/macro headwinds worsening.
